examples.en: Our company is diversifying its export markets.

examples.ko: 한 나라에만 기대지 말고 거래처를 다변화해야 해요.
examples.en: Instead of relying on one country, we need to diversify our clients.

examples.ko: 요즘 많은 기업이 판매 방식을 다변화하고 있어요.
examples.en: These days many companies are diversifying their ways of selling.
If you diversify import routes, the risk goes down.
The government decided to diversify its energy sources.
After the shop diversified its products, more customers came.

explain: '다양하게 하다'와 비슷하지만 수출, 시장, 투자, 공급처 같은 경제 이야기에서 주로 써요. 보통 '시장을 다변화하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 쓰고, 일상 대화보다는 뉴스나 회의에서 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It is close to 'making something varied', but it is mainly used in economic contexts such as markets, exports, investments and suppliers. It usually takes an object, as in '시장을 다변화하다', and is heard more in news and meetings than in casual talk.

examples.ko: 할머니는 자식과 손주가 많아서 다복하게 사세요.
examples.en: My grandmother has many children and grandchildren and lives a blessed life.
I envy my friend who grew up in a happy, blessed family.
I hope you are always healthy and blessed in the new year.
Looking at the family photo, you seem truly blessed.

examples.ko: 두 분은 자녀 복도 많고 참 다복해요.
examples.en: They are lucky in their children and truly fortunate.
The family is known for being blessed, so it is lively every holiday.

explain: 주로 가족이나 집안에 대해 '식구도 많고 복도 많다'는 느낌으로 써요. 덕담이나 인사말에서 자주 쓰고, 그냥 '행복하다'보다 조금 격식 있고 어른들이 즐겨 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for families or households, with the feeling of having many family members and many blessings. It often appears in good-wish greetings and sounds a little more formal and older-generation than a plain '행복하다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 몸집은 작아도 정말 다부져요.
examples.en: That player is small but really tough.
I walked into the interview room with a determined look.
My younger sibling made up their mind firmly and started studying.

examples.ko: 아이가 말하는 게 어찌나 다부진지 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The child spoke so firmly that I was surprised.

examples.ko: 다부져 보이는 체격이라 운동을 오래 했나 봐요.
examples.en: He has a sturdy build, so he must have exercised for a long time.
The youngest is known for being tough, so I do not worry.

explain: '튼튼하다'는 건강하고 잘 망가지지 않는 느낌이고, '다부지다'는 몸이나 태도가 꽉 짜여서 약해 보이지 않는 느낌이에요. '야무지다'는 일 처리가 빈틈없을 때 더 잘 어울려요. 몸집이 작은데 의외로 단단하거나 어린 사람이 당찰 때도 써요. 칭찬하는 말이에요.
explain_en: '튼튼하다' suggests healthy and not easily broken, while '다부지다' suggests a body or attitude that is tightly built and does not look weak. '야무지다' fits better when someone handles tasks without gaps. It also fits a small person who is surprisingly solid, or a young person who is spirited. It is a compliment.

examples.ko: 그 사고는 사람의 실수일 가능성이 다분해요.
examples.en: There is a strong possibility that the accident was human error.

examples.ko: 이번 발표는 투자자를 의식한 다분히 의도적인 선택이었어요.
examples.en: This announcement was a quite deliberate choice made with investors in mind.
It was a rather emotional reaction, but I can understand it.

examples.ko: 그 영화에는 오해를 살 만한 요소가 다분한 것 같아요.
examples.en: That movie seems to have plenty of elements that could cause misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 이대로 가면 실패할 소지가 다분하니까 계획을 바꿔요.
examples.en: If we go on like this, failure is quite likely, so let's change the plan.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 리더가 될 자질이 다분해 보여요.
examples.en: That friend seems to have plenty of leadership qualities.

explain: '가능성이 다분하다', '소지가 다분하다'처럼 그럴 만한 요소가 충분히 있다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '다분히'는 '꽤, 상당히'처럼 쓰여서 '다분히 의도적인'처럼 말해요. 주로 글이나 뉴스, 격식 있는 자리에서 들려요.
explain_en: It is most often used as in '가능성이 다분하다' or '소지가 다분하다', meaning the elements for something are clearly present. The adverb '다분히' works like 'quite' or 'considerably', as in '다분히 의도적인'. It is mostly found in writing, news and formal settings.

examples.en: This year was truly an eventful one.
After two eventful years, I am finally graduating.
Our family history has really been full of ups and downs.
The wedding preparations were so eventful that I was overwhelmed.

examples.ko: 다사다난하게 보낸 한 해를 정리해 봤어요.
examples.en: I looked back over the eventful year I went through.
It had its share of trouble, but it was an enjoyable trip.

explain: 연말 인사나 뉴스에서 '다사다난했던 한 해'라고 자주 말해요. 단순히 바쁜 게 아니라 일도 많고 어려움도 있었다는 느낌이라 '바쁘다'와 달라요. 주로 한 해, 시절, 인생 같은 긴 시간에 써요.
explain_en: People often say '다사다난했던 한 해' in year-end greetings and news. It is not just 'busy': it means many things happened, including difficulties. It is mainly used for long periods such as a year, an era or a life.

examples.en: The child is sitting quietly and demurely on the chair.
She sat demurely with her legs together.
The bride bowed her head modestly and greeted everyone.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어른들 말씀을 다소곳이 들었어요.
examples.en: That child listened meekly to what the adults said.

examples.ko: 꾸중을 들은 동생이 다소곳이 서 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling, who got scolded, is standing there quietly.

examples.ko: 손을 모은 채 다소곳이 차례를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: With hands folded, I waited my turn quietly.

explain: 앉다, 서다, 고개를 숙이다, 듣다처럼 조용한 동작과 자주 함께 써요. 얌전하고 공손한 태도를 그릴 때 쓰는 말이라, 소리 내지 않고 조용히 있는 모습에 어울려요.
explain_en: It often goes with quiet actions such as sitting, standing, bowing the head and listening. It paints a gentle, respectful attitude, so it suits someone who stays calm and quiet.

examples.ko: 다소곳한 모습으로 앉아 있는 아이가 귀여워요.
examples.en: The child sitting so demurely is cute.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 다소곳해서 호감이 가요.
examples.en: She speaks so gently that I like her.
In front of elders, you should behave modestly.
She looks meek, but she is strong inside.
Her bowed head looked so demure.
The child who had been so quiet suddenly laughed loudly.

explain: '얌전하다'와 비슷하지만, 고개를 조금 숙이고 말없이 온순한 모습을 그릴 때 더 잘 어울려요. 씩씩하고 활발한 사람에게는 잘 쓰지 않고, 보통 태도나 모습을 칭찬하듯 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '얌전하다', but fits best when picturing someone with a slightly lowered head and a quiet, gentle manner. It is rarely used for lively, energetic people and usually describes a manner or appearance in a complimentary way.

examples.en: The majority party passed the bill in the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 이번 선거에서 어느 당이 다수당을 차지할까요?
examples.en: Which party will win the majority in this election?

examples.ko: 다수당은 위원장 자리도 더 많이 가져가요.
examples.en: The majority party also takes more committee chair positions.
The policy stalled because of the majority party's opposition.
The minority party and the majority party are meeting to negotiate today.

examples.ko: 새 대통령은 다수당과 사이가 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: The new president is not on good terms with the majority party.

explain: 반대말은 '소수당'이에요. 국회 의석이 많은 정당을 말하고, 주로 뉴스나 선거 이야기에서 '다수당이 되다', '다수당을 차지하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '소수당' (minority party). It refers to the party with more seats in the legislature and appears in news and election talk, as in '다수당이 되다' or '다수당을 차지하다'.

examples.en: As a child, I caught freshwater snails in the stream.
Freshwater snails live only in clean water.
There are so many snails along the stream.
The kids looked at the snails and the tadpoles.
Soup made with freshwater snails tastes refreshing.

examples.ko: 다슬기 수제비를 먹어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever tried freshwater snail sujebi?

explain: 강이나 개울에 사는 작은 고둥으로, 국이나 수제비 재료로 먹어요. 지역에 따라 '올갱이'라고 부르는 곳도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a small freshwater snail living in rivers and streams, eaten in soup or sujebi. In some regions people call it '올갱이'.

examples.en: The diversification of values is progressing quickly.
Opinions have become more varied because of the pluralization of society.
Thanks to the pluralization of media, there is more to watch.

examples.ko: 공급처 다원화를 위해 여러 나라와 협력하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to cooperate with several countries to diversify our sources.

examples.ko: 다원화는 좋지만 갈등도 늘어날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Pluralization is good, but conflicts may increase too.
We had a discussion about the pluralization of education.

explain: '다양화'와 비슷하지만 다원화는 중심이나 가치, 체계가 하나가 아니라 여러 개가 된다는 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '일원화'예요. 주로 사회, 문화, 미디어 이야기에서 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '다양화', but 다원화 suggests that centers, values or systems become multiple rather than one. The opposite is '일원화'. It is mainly used when talking about society, culture and media.

examples.en: That writer is famous for being prolific.
Given how much they produce, the quality is high too.

examples.ko: 다작은 좋지만 질도 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: Producing a lot is good, but you must care about quality too.

examples.ko: 한 해에 영화를 세 편이나 찍다니 다작이네요.
examples.en: Shooting three films in a year, that is really prolific.
That singer tends to release a lot of work.

examples.ko: 다작 덕분에 팬들이 늘 새 노래를 기다려요.
examples.en: Thanks to their large output, fans always have new songs to look forward to.

explain: 작가, 화가, 감독, 가수처럼 작품을 만드는 사람에게 써요. 반대말은 '과작'이에요. 칭찬일 때도 있지만 '많이 만들면 질이 떨어지지 않을까' 하는 뉘앙스로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for people who create works, such as writers, painters, directors and singers. The opposite is '과작'. It can be praise, but sometimes it carries a hint of worry that quality may suffer.

examples.ko: 이번 시험에 떨어지고 나서 다시금 마음을 다잡았어요.
examples.en: After failing this exam, I pulled myself together once more.
I will steady my scattered mind and start studying.
You have to keep your focus to avoid mistakes.
I take a walk every morning to steady my mind.
Since it is a new year, I decided to renew my resolve.
The team leader pulled the wavering team back together.

explain: '마음을 다잡다'가 가장 흔한 쓰임이고, 정신, 자세, 분위기 같은 말과도 같이 써요. 흐트러진 것을 다시 단단히 바로잡는 느낌이라, 그냥 '잡다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: The most common use is '마음을 다잡다', and it also goes with words like spirit, posture and atmosphere. It feels like firmly re-steadying something that had loosened, which differs from plain '잡다'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 다혈질이라 금방 화를 내세요.
examples.en: Our team leader is hot-tempered and gets angry quickly.

examples.ko: 다혈질인 사람과 일하면 눈치를 보게 돼요.
examples.en: Working with a hot-tempered person makes you watch their mood.
I have a hot temper, so it is hard for me to hold back.

examples.ko: 그는 다혈질 성격 때문에 손해를 많이 봤어요.
examples.en: He lost out a lot because of his hot temper.

examples.ko: 다혈질은 아니지만 그 말에는 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I am not hot-tempered, but those words made me angry.

examples.ko: 다혈질의 형은 작은 일에도 소리를 질러요.
examples.en: My hot-tempered older brother shouts even over small things.

explain: 쉽게 흥분하고 화를 잘 내는 성격을 말하고, 보통 부정적으로 써요. '성격이 급하다'는 일을 서두르는 느낌이고, 다혈질은 감정이 확 올라와서 화내는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes a personality that gets excited and angry easily, and it is usually negative. '성격이 급하다' is about rushing things, while 다혈질 is about emotions flaring up into anger.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마니까 더 큰 방을 골랐어요.
examples.en: If the price is the same, you might as well take the better one, so I chose the bigger room.

examples.ko: 가격이 같으면 다홍치마라고 색이 예쁜 쪽을 샀어요.
examples.en: Since the price was the same, I bought the prettier-colored one.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마라서 포장이 좋은 선물을 골랐어요.
examples.en: As the price was the same, I picked the gift with nicer wrapping.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마인데 왜 그걸 안 사요?
examples.en: If it costs the same, why not buy the better one?

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마지요, 이왕이면 새 걸로 해요.
examples.en: Same price, so go for the better one. Let's get a new one.

examples.ko: 같은 값이면 다홍치마라는 말처럼 보기 좋은 상품이 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: As the saying goes, good-looking products are more popular.

explain: 거의 항상 속담 '같은 값이면 다홍치마'로 써요. 값이 같다면 겉모습이나 조건이 더 좋은 쪽을 고른다는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '이왕이면'과 비슷하게 가볍게 써요.

phrases.example: 같은 값이면 다홍치마라는데, 이왕이면 색이 예쁜 걸 사요.
phrases.en: They say if it costs the same, get the nicer one, so let's buy the prettier color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이 같을 때 더 좋은 쪽을 고르자는 속담이에요. 치마 이야기가 아니라 물건, 선택 전반에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that when the price is equal, choose the better option. It is not about skirts but about any choice.
phrases.en_equiv: may as well get the better one

explain_en: It is almost always used inside the proverb '같은 값이면 다홍치마'. It means that if the price is the same, you pick the one that looks or is better. In speech it works lightly, much like '이왕이면'.

examples.en: Mom keeps nagging me to do my homework.

examples.ko: 아무리 닦달해도 거래처의 답장은 쉽게 오지 않았어요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I pressed, the client's reply did not come easily.

examples.ko: 상사의 닦달에 지쳐서 퇴근 후에도 마음이 편하지 않아요.
examples.en: I am worn out by my boss's pushing, so I cannot relax even after work.

examples.ko: 너무 닦달하지 말고 조금만 기다려 주세요.
examples.en: Please do not push so hard and wait a little.
The department head pressed us to hand in the report quickly.
Please stop pushing me. I will handle it myself.

explain: '재촉하다'보다 훨씬 강하게 몰아붙이고 괴롭히는 느낌이라 보통 불만이 담겨요. '닦달'이라는 명사로도 많이 쓰고, 주로 '닦달을 받다', '닦달에 지치다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '재촉하다', carrying the sense of pressing and hounding someone, so it usually implies complaint. The noun '닦달' is also common, as in '닦달을 받다' or '닦달에 지치다'.

examples.en: Last night I had a truly sweet dream.
The newlyweds are still lost in sweet dreams.
The sweet dream of passing did not last long.
The sweet dream broke and reality began.
I woke from the sweet dream of the trip and went back to work.
The dreamlike time passed in an instant.

explain: 잠잘 때 꾸는 꿈보다 행복한 기대나 희망을 비유하는 말로 더 많이 써요. '단꿈을 꾸다', '단꿈에 젖다'처럼 말하고, 반대말은 '악몽'이에요.
explain_en: It is used more often as a metaphor for happy hopes and expectations than for an actual dream while sleeping. It appears as '단꿈을 꾸다' or '단꿈에 젖다', and the opposite is '악몽' (nightmare).

examples.en: This exam has a lot of short-answer questions.
Please answer briefly in a short-answer style.

examples.ko: 단답식은 정확한 단어를 알아야 풀 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only solve short-answer questions if you know the exact word.

examples.ko: 서술형보다 단답식이 더 쉬운 것 같아요.
examples.en: Short-answer questions seem easier than essay ones.

examples.ko: 면접에서 단답식 대답만 했더니 분위기가 어색했어요.
examples.en: I only gave one-word answers in the interview, and it felt awkward.
For the short-answer questions, I only replied 'yes' or 'no'.

explain: 시험에서는 보기를 고르는 '객관식', 길게 쓰는 '서술형'과 구분해요. 시험 말고도 말을 짧게만 대답하는 모습을 '단답식으로 대답하다'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '단답형'도 써요.
explain_en: On exams it is distinguished from multiple choice ('객관식') and long-form writing ('서술형'). Outside exams, '단답식으로 대답하다' describes giving only short replies in conversation. '단답형' is a similar term.
